summary: Rodeo sits on a narrow shelf of land along the eastern shore of San Pablo Bay, and from its hillside streets you can watch container ships glide through the Carquinez Strait while fog pours over the ridgeline — a working waterfront panorama most Bay Area residents never think to look for. The town's physical footprint is shaped almost entirely by the Phillips 66 refinery (now transitioning to a renewable fuels facility), which has been the economic anchor for over a century and still dominates the southern end of the community; beyond it, the terrain climbs steeply into grassy coastal hills laced with fire roads and informal trails connecting to the broader East Bay Regional Park system. At 4.6 square miles with under 9,000 people, this is functionally a bedroom community — Interstate 80 and the Hercules Transit Center funnel commuters toward Richmond, Oakland, and San Francisco, a corridor that can stretch well past an hour in peak traffic. A median home price around $652,000 against a median household income near $89,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 7:1, meaning purchasing requires substantial savings or dual incomes even at the median. The commercial strip along San Pablo Avenue offers scattered fast-casual spots and convenience retail but no real walkable downtown core, and the community can feel bisected by the freeway and industrial infrastructure rather than knit together. Rodeo is a place where bay views and refinery stacks coexist in the same sightline — an unusual compression of natural beauty and heavy industry that defines its essential character.
